s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with intermittent throbbing and localization to the right lower quadrant, associated with nausea and increased stool frequency, and a complex medical history
salient_findings: Intermittent throbbing abdominal pain localizing to the right lower quadrant
Moderate tenderness in the right lower quadrant and positive Rovsing sign
Lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve on CT
No appendix identified on CT or laparoscopy
Biopsy showing acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis
Small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum on repeat CT
key_facts: 49-year-old Caucasian woman
5-day history of abdominal pain
Pain began periumbilically and localized to the right lower quadrant
Associated with nausea and increased stool frequency
History of laparoscopic cholecystectomy in 2009
History of supracervical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy for uterine fibroids in 2012
Endometriosis noted during previous surgery
Moderate tenderness in the right lower quadrant on examination
Positive Rovsing sign
Normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count
Contrast-enhanced CT showed lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve
Appendix not identified on CT or laparoscopy
Biopsy of inflamed areas showed acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis
Patient improved initially but returned with sharp right lower quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting
Repeat white-cell count was 13.2×10^9/L
Repeat CT showed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of abdominal pain localizing to the right lower quadrant, positive Rovsing sign, and initial CT findings

shortlist.label: Endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of endometriosis, biopsy showing foci of endometriosis, and symptoms consistent with intestinal endometriosis

shortlist.label: Small-bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Repeat CT showing small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum and clinical presentation of sharp pain, nausea, and vomiting

shortlist.label: Intestinal endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings and clinical presentation consistent with endometriosis involving the intestines

shortlist.label: Neoplastic small-bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Complex medical history and CT findings suggesting a possible mass, raising concern for a neoplastic cause of obstruction

raw.rationale: The patient's history of endometriosis, the presence of foci of endometriosis on biopsy of inflamed areas, and the location of the inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve support this diagnosis, which can cause bowel obstruction and mimic appendicitis.

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: The appendix was not identified on CT or laparoscopy, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Endometriosis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of endometriosis, this option is too broad and does not specifically address the intestinal involvement.

rejected.label: Small-bowel obstruction
rejected.why: This is a symptom rather than a specific diagnosis, and the underlying cause of the obstruction needs to be identified.

rejected.label: Neoplastic small-bowel obstruction
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of a neoplasm on the CT scans or biopsy results, making this diagnosis less likely.
